title: Tabuk, and Ka'b's honesty
hook: He had no excuse for staying home. Everyone else lied. He told the truth, and waited fifty days.

screens.text: **He had no excuse for staying home.** Over eighty men talked their way out of trouble. Ka'b ibn Malik told the plain truth, and then waited fifty long nights for Allah's answer.

**A march in the heat.** In 9 AH, in fierce heat, the Prophet ﷺ led a large army to Tabuk to meet a Byzantine threat. In the end, IslamQA reports, no battle took place [IslamQA 11575; IslamQA 305386].
bubbles: Ka'b ibn Malik meant to go. He said later he had never been stronger or richer: for the first time in his life he owned two camels [Bukhari 4418].

screens.prompt: How did Ka'b end up staying behind? Put his story in order [Bukhari 4418].
items: He has everything he needs to go
Each morning he sets out to prepare, and comes home with nothing done
The army leaves, and he tells himself he'll catch up
screens.feedback: No big decision, just one small delay after another. Ka'b told it honestly himself [Bukhari 4418].

screens.text: **The excuse makers.** When the Prophet ﷺ came home, over eighty men who had stayed behind came with excuses and swore oaths. He accepted what they said and left their hearts to Allah [Bukhari 4418].
bubbles: Ka'b was a gifted speaker. He knew he could talk his way out, and he knew a lie wouldn't stay hidden from Allah [Bukhari 4418].

events.title: Hunayn
events.text: A valley ambush, and the Ansar reassured [Bukhari 4330].

events.title: The march to Tabuk
events.text: Fierce heat, a long road. No battle takes place, IslamQA reports [IslamQA 11575].

events.title: Ka'b tells the truth
events.text: Others make excuses. Ka'b says he had none [Bukhari 4418].

events.title: The wait
events.text: No one speaks to Ka'b and two others [Bukhari 4418].

screens.text: **The plain truth.** Ka'b sat in front of him and said it straight: I had no excuse. I was never stronger or richer than when I stayed behind. The Prophet ﷺ said this man had told the truth, and to wait for Allah's decision [Bukhari 4418].

cards.back: The Muslims were told not to speak to Ka'b and two others. Even his cousin and dearest friend wouldn't answer his greeting. Ka'b wept [Bukhari 4418].
A letter came from a foreign king: you're being treated badly, come join us. Ka'b saw it as another test and burned it [Bukhari 4418].
On the fiftieth morning, after Fajr, a voice called from a hill: Ka'b, good news! He fell down in prostration [Bukhari 4418].

screens.text: **The way back.** Allah forgave *"the three who were left alone"*, then *"turned to them so they could repent"* [Q 9:118, Saheeh Intl.]. The Prophet's ﷺ face shone with joy. Rejoice, he told Ka'b: it's your best day since you were born [Bukhari 4418].
bubbles: Slipped since becoming Muslim? Honesty about it is the door back, not the end. Ka'b's way is open to you too.

screens.situation: Luis hasn't prayed Fajr in two weeks and skipped his last two classes at the masjid. His mentor texts: "How are your prayers going?" Luis feels embarrassed.

options.text: Tell the truth: he's been struggling, and he'd like help getting back on track
options.feedback: Yes. Like Ka'b: the plain truth, then the way back. A good mentor will help, not judge.

options.text: Say work has been crazy, so he's been making them up later
options.feedback: Not quite. A small excuse buys a little comfort and blocks the help he needs [Bukhari 6094].

options.text: Leave the message on read and avoid the mentor
options.feedback: Not quite. Hiding makes the gap wider. Ka'b went and faced it, and relief came.

chips: Why were Ka'b and the others not spoken to?
What is tawbah, and how do I do it?
I've slipped. How do I come back?

screens.prompt: Is there something you've been making excuses about, to yourself or to Allah? What would the plain truth sound like?

screens.text: Tell the plain truth once today.
steps: Name one thing you've been putting off or excusing
Tell Allah about it honestly in a short du'a
Take one small step back toward it before tomorrow

screens.text: Ka'b had a smooth excuse ready and chose the truth. Honesty about your failures is the way back to Allah, every time.
Next episode: the Year of Delegations. Tribe after tribe arrives in Madinah, and a captive chief changes his mind.

check.prompt: What did Ka'b say when he faced the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: That he had no excuse at all
options.feedback: Right. He told the plain truth, then waited for Allah's decision [Bukhari 4418].
Not quite. Others made excuses. Ka'b admitted he had never been stronger or richer [Bukhari 4418].

check.prompt: How did Ka'b's fifty nights end?

options.text: Allah accepted his repentance, and the Prophet ﷺ rejoiced
options.feedback: Right. Allah turned to the three so they could repent [Q 9:117–118; Bukhari 4418].
Not quite. He burned the offer to leave, waited, and was forgiven [Bukhari 4418].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- In 9 AH, in intense heat, he led a large army to Tabuk to meet a Byzantine threat; no battle took place; it was his last campaign [IslamQA 11575; IslamQA 305386; the heat and long journey also in Bukhari 4418]. Say "a large army" (30,000 is sirah only). No battle, but the Day 71 frame still applies to questions about fighting. (scholar question Q39)
- Ka'b ibn Malik (who had been at the pledge of 'Aqabah) stayed behind with no excuse: he had never been stronger or wealthier, owned two camels for the first time, and kept putting off preparing until the army was gone [Bukhari 4418].
- On the Prophet's ﷺ return, over eighty men who had stayed behind made excuses and swore oaths; he accepted their outward word, asked forgiveness for them, and left their hearts to Allah. Ka'b, a fluent speaker, told the truth: he had no excuse. The Prophet ﷺ said he had told the truth and to wait for Allah's decision [Bukhari 4418].
- Ka'b, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah were not spoken to for fifty nights; even Ka'b's cousin Abu Qatadah didn't return his greeting; a letter from the king of Ghassan invited Ka'b to join him, and he burned it; on the fiftieth morning after Fajr a man called the good news from the hill of Sal'; Ka'b fell in prostration, gave the messenger his clothes, and the Prophet ﷺ, his face shining, told him it was his best day since his mother bore him [Bukhari 4418].
- Allah forgave the Prophet ﷺ, the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and the three who were left behind, turning to them so they could repent [Q 9:117–118]. Ka'b resolved to speak only the truth for the rest of his life [Bukhari 4418].

**Likely questions**
- *"Why were they boycotted? Do Muslims shun people today?"* It was a specific, temporary discipline by the Prophet ﷺ himself, pending revelation, and it ended in forgiveness and joy. It is not a model for believers shunning each other today. Don't encourage the convert to shun anyone; questions about cutting people off go to the imam.
- *"Who were the excuse makers?"* The hadith calls them people who stayed behind and swore excuses; the Qur'an (Surah al-Tawbah) speaks of hypocrites. Don't label anyone today a hypocrite.
- *"I've slipped. How do I come back?"* Warmly: struggling isn't leaving Islam. Tawbah is honest regret, stopping, and returning; Allah accepts repentance [Q 9:118]. Point to Day 62 and the welcome-back modules. Suggest one small step and the mentor. Never shame.
- *"What is tawbah?"* Turning back to Allah: admit it, regret it, stop, and resolve to do better; then keep going.

**Escalate:** a convert who sounds hopeless, ashamed to the point of crisis, or considering leaving Islam (mentor; safety rule if needed); questions about shunning or excommunication (imam).

**Don't**
- Don't use the boycott to suggest Allah or the community will reject a struggling convert.
- Don't present shunning as something Muslims do to each other today.
- Don't call anyone a hypocrite.
